sections.heading: Austra College: Vocational Educational and Training Courses > Frequently Asked Questions > Do you offer financial assistance or payment plans?

blocks.text: Austra College does not offer government-funded courses; however, we provide flexible payment options. Students can pay their tuition fees through easy weekly, fortnightly, or monthly instalments, making study more accessible and manageable.

sections.heading: Austra College: Vocational Educational and Training Courses > Frequently Asked Questions > Where do I find application closing dates?

blocks.text: Application closing dates and intake information are available on our social website at austra.edu.au . You may also contact our admissions team directly using the phone numbers listed on the website for assistance.

sections.heading: Austra College: Vocational Educational and Training Courses > Frequently Asked Questions > Who are the lecturers and tutors?

blocks.text: Our lecturers and trainers are highly experienced industry professionals with strong practical knowledge in their respective fields. They bring real-world expertise into the classroom to ensure high-quality learning outcomes.

sections.heading: Austra College: Vocational Educational and Training Courses > Frequently Asked Questions > Can I study part-time?

blocks.text: Yes. Austra College offers part-time study options across selected courses, allowing students to balance their education with work and personal commitments.

sections.heading: Austra College: Vocational Educational and Training Courses > Frequently Asked Questions > Do you offer weekend or evening classes?

blocks.text: Yes. We provide flexible study schedules, including weekend classes, evening classes, and weekday morning sessions, depending on course availability and campus schedules.

sections.heading: Austra College: Vocational Educational and Training Courses > Frequently Asked Questions > Do you offer practical training or only theory-based classes?

blocks.text: Austra College delivers a combination of theoretical learning and practical hands-on training. Our programs are designed with modern tools, equipment, and experiential learning methods to ensure students gain real industry-ready skills.

sections.heading: Austra College: Vocational Educational and Training Courses > Frequently Asked Questions > Do you organise excursions or student events?

blocks.text: Yes. We regularly organise weekly, monthly, and annual events and activities across campuses. These events help build community engagement, enhance student experience, and encourage networking and participation.

sections.heading: About the course

blocks.text: ELICOS stands for English Language Intensive Courses for Overseas Students. At Austra College, General English helps you practise the language used when living, studying and interacting in an English-speaking environment. Lessons bring the four core language skills together with grammar, vocabulary and pronunciation. You will be placed in a level suited to your English proficiency. As you progress, you will work with more challenging language and practise expressing your ideas in a wider range of situations.

sections.heading: What you will learn What you will learn > Speaking and pronunciation

blocks.text: Practice introducing yourself, asking questions, sharing opinions, and participating in conversations. Develop clearer pronunciation through speaking activities and feedback.

sections.heading: What you will learn What you will learn > Listening

blocks.text: Build your understanding of spoken English through conversations, recordings and classroom activities, progressing to more complex content at higher levels.

sections.heading: What you will learn What you will learn > Reading

blocks.text: Develop strategies to understand everyday information and longer texts. Practice identifying main ideas, finding details and interpreting meaning.

sections.heading: What you will learn What you will learn > Writing

blocks.text: Build from simple sentences and personal messages to connected, structured texts. Practice organising your ideas and using grammar and vocabulary appropriately.

sections.heading: Six levels of English

blocks.text: Each level is designed to be completed over 10 teaching weeks. The placement descriptions below follow our course entry framework. Your placement test and interview help identify the appropriate starting level.

rows: Little or no exposure to English
CEFR A1 — basic understanding of English
CEFR B1 — everyday conversations and familiar topics
CEFR B2 — complex communication and discussions
CEFR C1 — high fluency and comprehension
blocks.text:
Level | Placement guide | Duration
Beginner | Little or no exposure to English | 10 weeks
Elementary | CEFR A1 — basic understanding of English | 10 weeks
Pre-Intermediate | CEFR A2 — foundational English skills | 10 weeks
Intermediate | CEFR B1 — everyday conversations and familiar topics | 10 weeks
Upper-Intermediate | CEFR B2 — complex communication and discussions | 10 weeks
Advanced | CEFR C1 — high fluency and comprehension | 10 weeks

sections.heading: How you will study

blocks.text: You will attend 20 hours of face-to-face classes each week and complete a minimum of 5 hours of independent study. The full curriculum contains 60 weekly units of study , supported by Headway coursebooks, workbooks and supplementary learning materials. Lessons combine teacher-led instruction with discussions, role-plays, oral presentations, individual tasks and group activities. Audio-visual resources, web-based research and authentic everyday materials give you opportunities to use English in practical contexts.

sections.heading: Entry requirements

blocks.text: You must be 18 years of age or older to enrol. No formal educational qualifications are required, although most students are expected to have completed Year 10 or equivalent. Placement is based on English proficiency rather than previous academic achievement. Upon arrival, you will complete an English placement test and an individual interview. The curriculum specifies the Oxford Placement Test. Where applicable, recognised English test results, including IELTS, Cambridge, PTE or TOEFL, may also inform placement decisions.

sections.heading: Assessment and progression

blocks.text: Your teachers will monitor your progress through written and spoken activities, regular mini-tests and individual feedback. Mini-tests take place in Weeks 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8 and 9 of each level , with mid-term and end-of-term assessments in Weeks 5 and 10. The course specifies a minimum pass requirement of 50% in the mid-term and end-of-term assessments for progression. Teachers record your results and provide targeted feedback and additional support where needed. After completing all enrolled levels, you will receive a certificate highlighting your achievements.

sections.heading: Support while you study

blocks.text: Our teaching approach takes into account different learning styles, cultural backgrounds, and learning needs. Support is provided for students experiencing difficulties.

sections.heading: Support while you study > Additional Assistance

blocks.text: Progress and attendance are reviewed during each term. Students are expected to maintain at least 80% attendance and participate in required assessments. Students at risk of falling behind receive support through the college’s intervention process.

sections.heading: Course fees

The weekly resource fee is additional to tuition. Contact our admissions team for your enrolment fee details and payment information.

sections.heading: Further study options

blocks.text: General English can help you develop language skills for further English study, including English for Academic Purposes, vocational education and training, or higher education. Entry to any further course depends on meeting that course’s admission and English language requirements. Completion does not guarantee admission or employment.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions

blocks.text: 1. Who can study General English

The course is designed for learners aged 18 and over who want to improve their English for everyday communication and social interactions. It caters for a range of abilities, from Beginner to Advanced.
2. Do I need to be confident in English before starting
No. The Beginner level is designed for learners with little or no exposure to English. Your placement test and interview will help determine the level that suits you.
3. How long is the course

The complete six-level curriculum contains 60 structured teaching weeks, with 10 teaching weeks per level. The course structure also lists 10 weeks of breaks. Your enrolment documentation will set out your study dates and enrolled levels.
4. Where can I study
General English is offered across all Austra College locations: Melbourne, Sydney, Adelaide and Perth.
5. What does the weekly fee include
The weekly course fee is AUD $300. A separate weekly resource fee of AUD $40 and a one-time application fee of AUD $400 also apply.
6. Is this a dual qualification
No. General English is offered as a single course. Its CRICOS Course Code is 121349J.
7. When can I start
Contact our admissions team for upcoming intake dates and class arrangements at your preferred campus.

How fast will someone actually respond?

sections.heading: Why do trade courses in Australia have such strong job outcomes?

blocks.text: Employers across construction, hospitality, automotive, and engineering are having real difficulty finding qualified staff. Jobs and Skills Australia’s 2025 Occupation Shortage List found that Technicians and Trades Workers make up the largest share of the country’s persistent occupational shortages, and trade vacancies are being filled at a noticeably lower rate than the national average — employers are advertising these roles and simply not getting enough suitable applicants.

The training itself holds up under scrutiny too. NCVER’s most recent VET student outcomes survey found that most graduates finish with an improved employment status, achieve the training goal they set out to reach, and report being satisfied with the course. That combination — real demand from employers plus training that reliably does what it says — is what makes a Certificate III trade qualification a genuinely practical choice, not just a marketing line.

sections.heading: What are VET courses in Australia?

blocks.text: VET (Vocational Education and Training) is Australia’s national system of practical, industry-linked qualifications delivered by registered training organisations — assessed on units of competency rather than exams. 5.1 million domestic and international students were enrolled in nationally recognised VET in 2025 (NCVER).

sections.heading: What are VET courses in Australia? > Nationally recognised

blocks.text: A qualification earned in Perth is valid in Brisbane, Darwin or Hobart. Course codes (SIT, CPC, AUR, ICT, BSB, MSF) are set nationally, not by individual colleges.

sections.heading: What are VET courses in Australia? > AQF-aligned

blocks.text: Each qualification sits at a defined level on the Australian Qualifications Framework — Certificate III (AQF 3) through to Graduate Diploma (AQF 8).

sections.heading: What are VET courses in Australia? > Regulated

blocks.text: RTOs are audited by the Australian Skills Quality Authority (ASQA). Courses delivered to international students must also be registered on CRICOS.

sections.heading: What’s the difference between a VET course and a trade course?

blocks.text: Every trade course is a VET course, but not every VET course is a trade course. A trade course trains you for a specific hands-on occupation — carpenter, chef, motor mechanic, roof plumber, cabinet maker, bricklayer — typically at Certificate III level with substantial practical assessment. A non-trade VET course, like the BSB50420 Diploma of Leadership and Management, builds professional capability without tying you to one on-tools occupation. ELICOS General English sits outside the VET system entirely — it’s a separately regulated English language program, not a nationally recognised VET qualification.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions > What courses does Austra College offer in Australia?

blocks.text: Austra College offers 25 courses in total: 24 nationally recognised VET qualifications across seven training packages — Hospitality (SIT), Construction (CPC), Automotive (AUR), Information Technology (ICT), Leadership and Management (BSB), Furniture Making (MSF) and Engineering (MEM) — from Certificate III through to Graduate Diploma, plus a six-level ELICOS General English program.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions > Which trade courses in Australia does Austra College deliver?

blocks.text: Austra College delivers trade qualifications including Certificate III in Carpentry, Painting and Decorating, Solid Plastering, Construction Waterproofing, Bricklaying and Blocklaying, Wall and Ceiling Lining, Joinery, Stonemasonry, Roof Plumbing, Commercial Cookery, Light Vehicle Mechanical Technology, Cabinet Making and Timber Technology, Glass and Glazing, and Engineering (Fabrication Trade), plus Certificate IV and Diploma-level progression qualifications. Wall and Ceiling Lining, Joinery, Stonemasonry, Roof Plumbing and Engineering (Fabrication Trade) are currently delivered only at the Melbourne and Sydney campuses.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions > Where can I study trade courses in Melbourne, Sydney, Perth or Adelaide?

blocks.text: Austra College has four campuses: Level 5/131 Queen Street Melbourne, Level 2/133 Parramatta Road Granville (Sydney), Level 2/440 William Street Perth, and Level 3/90 King William Street Adelaide. Most courses run at all four; five construction and engineering trade courses currently run only at the Melbourne and Sydney campuses.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions > Are Austra College courses nationally recognised?

blocks.text: Yes. Austra College is a registered training organisation (RTO Code: 40336) delivering nationally recognised qualifications aligned to the Australian Qualifications Framework and regulated by the Australian Skills Quality Authority.
Can international students enrol in trade courses in Melbourne?

Yes. Austra College is registered on CRICOS (CRICOS Code: 03187D). International students can enrol in CRICOS-registered trade courses in Melbourne and at our Sydney, Perth and Adelaide campuses, studying face-to-face and full-time on campus. Entry requirements vary by qualification — confirm on the individual course page.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions > Does Austra College offer English language courses?

blocks.text: Yes. Austra College offers ELICOS General English, a six-level program from Beginner to Advanced, at all four campuses — Melbourne, Sydney, Perth and Adelaide. ELICOS is an English language program, not a VET qualification, and is registered separately on CRICOS.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions > Do I need experience to start a trade course?

blocks.text: No, for Certificate III qualifications. Certificate III is a trade-entry level and assumes no prior trade qualification. Diploma, Advanced Diploma and Graduate Diploma courses typically expect prior study or relevant workplace experience.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions > How long does a trade course take?

blocks.text: Duration varies by qualification, campus and study load. Exact course duration is listed on each individual course page — check there or speak to a course advisor.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions > Does a trade qualification give me a licence to work?

blocks.text: Not automatically. Trade licensing and builder registration are administered separately by each state and territory regulator. A nationally recognised qualification is usually a prerequisite, but additional experience or licensing steps may apply.

Technology touches every industry in Australia, and it’s exactly why so many students look for a solid information and communication technology course to build a career around. Students build capability across advanced data management, cyber security, network engineering, systems development, and IT project and business management.

Rather than a generic computer course, this information and communication technology course is a specialist qualification — students build advanced, job-ready technical skills across these areas, using the same tools and platforms seen in professional IT environments.

sections.heading: ICT- Information and Communication Technology > Frequently Asked Questions > 4. Can international students study ICT courses at Austra College?

blocks.text: Yes. Austra College is CRICOS-registered (RTO Code: 40336 | CRICOS Code: 03187D) and approved to deliver nationally recognised training to international students, with campuses in Adelaide, Melbourne, Sydney, and Perth.

sections.heading: ICT- Information and Communication Technology > Frequently Asked Questions > 5. Is an ICT course only about coding?

blocks.text: No. Coding is just one part of the ICT field. This course also covers networking, cyber security, systems analysis, and IT project and business management, so students can build a career that isn’t purely programming-focused.

sections.heading: ICT- Information and Communication Technology > Frequently Asked Questions > 6. What can I do after completing the ICT course?

blocks.text: Graduates typically move into technical or supervisory IT roles, and may also continue into further study, such as a Graduate Certificate or Bachelor-level qualification, depending on the institution’s entry requirements.

sections.heading: ICT- Information and Communication Technology > Frequently Asked Questions > 7. Does completing an ICT course guarantee a job?

blocks.text: No. A qualification builds the skills and knowledge employers look for, but career outcomes depend on individual experience, the job market, and employer requirements at the time.

sections.heading: Overview

blocks.text: AUSTRA COLLEGE is committed to protecting the privacy of the personal information it collects and receives. This policy has been developed in accordance with the Australian Privacy Principles (APPs) in the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) (Privacy Act).

This policy explains how AUSTRA COLLEGE collects, uses, discloses and otherwise handles personal information relating to individuals. It also explains how you can ask to access and correct the personal information we hold about you or complain about any suspected privacy breach. Nothing in this policy limits any of our other obligations at law.
Collection of Personal Information
AUSTRA COLLEGE is required to collect personal information only by lawful and fair means. Where possible we will collect personal information we require directly from you.

Personal information we hold may include your name, current and previous addresses, telephone numbers, e-mail addresses, overseas contact details, emergency contacts, family details, visa details, passport details, your employer and employment details if provided directly by you and as relevant to our purposes, your preferences and interests as relevant to your enrolment or employment with AUSTRA COLLEGE, and any other information we require to perform our services to you. Further information may be collected with your consent in specific instances as notified to you.
Personal information entered into the AUSTRA COLLEGE database will not be used or disclosed by us, except as authorised by you or as is reasonably necessary for the purposes outlined to you.

Should you choose not to provide personal information we may not be able to provide you with the services, or may not be able to provide you with the services to a sufficient level that we regard as best practice.
We may collect personal information:
from the information supplied by you to AUSTRA COLLEGE, including as described in the analytics section below
in conversation and communication with you
from government departments that we associate with to enable us to offer our services
from third parties including employers, service providers, related companies or your representatives from publicly available sources of information
when we are required to do so by law
Where AUSTRA COLLEGE collects your personal information, AUSTRA COLLEGE will take reasonable steps to notify you of:
the purposes for which we are collecting the information
the third parties to whom we may disclose the information of that kind
whether any of those third parties are located overseas and, if practicable to specify, the countries in which they are located
how to access and correct personal information and make privacy complaints

AUSTRA COLLEGE will only collect sensitive information where it is reasonably necessary for our core functions or activities. For example, we may collect the following information for enrolment into qualifications that are on AUSTRA COLLEGE’s scope of registration as a Registered Training Organisation (RTO):
information about your previous education and employment experience
visa, passport and other immigration information
identification as Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander
English Language results
Agent details

Where it is practical and lawful for us to do so, AUSTRA COLLEGE will enable you to access our website and make general telephone enquiries without having to identify yourself or by using a pseudonym. AUSTRA COLLEGE also enables you to respond to our surveys anonymously.
Web Analytics
Cookies through the AUSTRA COLLEGE Website

Most internet browsers are set to accept cookies. If you prefer not to receive them, you can adjust your internet browser to reject cookies. Rejecting cookies can, however, limit the functionality of our website. There are a range of websites that provide tips on how to disable cookies. Here is an example: http://www.wikihow.com/Disable-Cookies . However please note that AUSTRA COLLEGE does not endorse the content of external websites. You are advised to refer to them at your discretion.
Web and Email Analytics

AUSTRA COLLEGE has enabled the Google Analytics Demographics and Interest Reporting functionality available through Google Analytics. AUSTRA COLLEGE and our associates use first-party cookies (Google Analytics cookies) and third-party cookies (the DoubleClick cookie) to collect information.

AUSTRA COLLEGE and its authorised service providers, use web beacons in conjunction with cookies to collect information that enables us to greater tailor our services to your interests and needs, such as your browsing activities and website and email clicks. Web beacons typically work in conjunction with cookies and are small graphic images that may be included in our sites or other communications and can identify our users and user behaviour. Our authorised service providers may also use information collected from your browsing activities to help us target relevant advertising on our website and other places on the Internet. These technologies assist AUSTRA COLLEGE to understand the usefulness of our offerings to you.

If you would like to opt-out of the collection of cookies and other technologies then follow the instructions above (in the ‘Cookies through the AUSTRA COLLEGE website’). This will instruct you on how to reject cookies. You can also find out more from Google.
Use and Disclosure of Personal Information
Your personal information may be used by us or our associates to:
provide products and services to you
collect payments and to administer your account
provide you with updated or new information about our products and services
for development of existing and new products and services
maintain and update our business infrastructure and systems
promote our other products and services to you
In providing our products and services, or collecting and using your personal information, your personal information may be disclosed to third party organisations including:
information technology service providers
marketing and communications agencies
mailing houses, freight and courier services
printers and distributors of direct marketing material
our legal, accounting, financial or other professional advisors
regulatory, government and other authorities as required by law
Opting Out
You can opt out of receiving marketing communications from AUSTRA COLLEGE at any time through the following channels:
By Mail: AUSTRA COLLEGE, Suite 2, Level 4, 97 Pirie Street, Adelaide SA 5000
By Email: info@austra.vetgpt.com.au
By telephone: +61 8 8410 9915
By utilising the unsubscribe facility that we include in our electronic messages such as emails and SMS
You agree and acknowledge that even if you opt out of receiving marketing material, we will still send you essential information that we are required to send you relating to the services we provide.
Unsolicited Information

Unsolicited personal information is personal information we receive that we have taken no active steps to collect. If the information we receive is not required for AUSTRA COLLEGE to perform one or more of our services, AUSTRA COLLEGE will destroy or de-identify the information as soon as practicable.
Quality of Personal Information

AUSTRA COLLEGE takes reasonable steps to make sure that the personal information we collect, use or disclose, is accurate, complete and up-to-date. However, the accuracy of that information depends to a large extent on the information you provide.
We recommend that you:
let us know if there are any errors in your personal information
keep us up-to-date with changes to your information
Security of Personal Information
We take reasonable steps to protect your personal information we hold from misuse, loss, unauthorised access, modification or disclosure.

You can also help to protect the privacy of your personal information by keeping passwords secret and by ensuring that you log out of the website when you have completed your transaction. If you become aware of any security breach, please contact AUSTRA COLLEGE head office as soon as possible.
We will take reasonable steps to destroy or permanently de-identify personal information if it is no longer needed for any purpose for which the information was intended.
AUSTRA COLLEGE is not responsible for the privacy or security of third party websites that you access via links on the AUSTRA COLLEGE website.
Access and Correction of your Personal Information

You are able to access your personal information that we hold, with some exceptions as allowed by law. To obtain a copy of your personal information, write to the AUSTRA COLLEGE Head Office requesting the information and we will assess your request and provide you with a response, usually within 10 working days. We reserve the right to charge a reasonable fee for the provision of this information. If we refuse your request, or if we refuse to give you access in the manner you requested, AUSTRA COLLEGE’s policy is to provide you with written confirmation of the reasons for our refusal and the available complaint process.

Students can access and update their contact details by logging into the WiseNet Student Portal. Students may also complete a Change of Details form, which is available for download on the AUSTRA COLLEGE website. For any personal information that can’t be accessed and corrected through the Student Portal, please contact AUSTRA COLLEGE head office.
Variation

This policy may be varied from time to time in accordance with any changes to our practices or changes to the way we collect, use and disclose any personal information. You should check this policy regularly so that you are aware of any variations made to this policy.
Complaints

If you have a complaint about how AUSTRA COLLEGE has collected, stored or used your personal information, please contact AUSTRA COLLEGE’s head office. We will endeavour to deal with your complaint and take any steps necessary to resolve the matter promptly, but usually within 10 business days.
If your complaint is unable to be resolved within 10 business days, AUSTRA COLLEGE will advise you in writing, including letting you know when we expect to provide our response.

If you are unhappy with our response, you can refer your complaint to the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner, whose contact details can be found here: https://www.oaic.gov.au/about-us/contact-us

Please contact AUSTRA COLLEGE if you have any queries about the personal information that AUSTRA COLLEGE holds about you, including the way we use or disclose that personal information, or if you wish to access or correct the personal information held by us or opt out of receiving our marketing communications. Our contact details are set out below.
Contact Us General Manager
Austra College Suite 2, Level 4 97 Pirie Street Adelaide SA 5000
T: +61 8 8410 9915 F: +61 8 8410 9916 E: info@austra.vetgpt.com.au

sections.heading: Overview

blocks.text: — Automotive Technology

sections.heading: Automotive Courses in Australia

blocks.text: Nationally recognised automotive course in Australia for international students — from light vehicle mechanical technology to automotive diagnosis, with hands-on training across Adelaide, Melbourne, Sydney, and Perth.
Enquire Now
View Intake Schedule

Australia’s automotive industry keeps evolving with new vehicle technology, and that’s exactly why international students search for a practical automotive course to build a trade career around. At Austra College, our automotive courses are delivered under the nationally recognised AUR Training Package, combining real workshop training with hands-on diagnostic and repair skills.

Whether you’re starting out with light vehicle mechanical technology or progressing toward automotive diagnosis, these courses are designed to take you from the workshop floor to a genuine trade career. Training is delivered across our Adelaide, Melbourne, Sydney, and Perth campuses.

sections.heading: Automotive Courses in Australia > Our Automotive Trade Courses in Australia

blocks.text: Austra College offers a clear, structured pathway through the automotive qualification levels — allowing students to start at the level that suits their experience and progress as far as they want to take their career.
Certificate III
AUR30620 – Certificate III in Light Vehicle Mechanical Technology
Foundational mechanical skills, vehicle servicing, and workshop safety. The entry point into a career as a qualified vehicle technician.
Learn more
Certificate IV
AUR40216 – Certificate IV in Automotive Mechanical Diagnosis
Advanced fault-finding and diagnostic skills for technicians moving into complex vehicle repair and diagnosis work.
Learn more
Diploma
AUR50216 – Diploma of Automotive Technology
Senior technical skills, workshop supervision, and advanced systems knowledge for technicians aiming for leadership roles.
Learn more
Course duration and unit selection vary and are reviewed periodically — please refer to each individual course page or speak with our admissions team for current details.

sections.heading: Automotive Courses in Australia > Our Automotive Trade Courses in Australia > AUR30620 – Certificate III in Light Vehicle Mechanical Technology

blocks.text: The Certificate III in Light Vehicle Mechanical Technology is the entry point into a career as a qualified automotive technician. Students learn essential workshop skills including vehicle servicing, engine systems, electrical basics, and workplace safety, delivered through practical training in a real workshop environment.

This course suits school leavers, career changers, and international students wanting to build the foundational skills needed to work as a technician in dealerships, repair shops, and service centres.
Learn more about AUR30620 – Certificate III in Light Vehicle Mechanical Technology →

sections.heading: Automotive Courses in Australia > Our Automotive Trade Courses in Australia > AUR40216 – Certificate IV in Automotive Mechanical Diagnosis

blocks.text: The Certificate IV in Automotive Mechanical Diagnosis builds on core mechanical skills with a focus on diagnosing complex vehicle faults. Students develop skills in engine management systems, electronic diagnostics, and advanced fault-finding techniques.
This qualification suits technicians with some industry experience who want to move into diagnostic or specialist repair roles.
Learn more about AUR40216 – Certificate IV in Automotive Mechanical Diagnosis →

sections.heading: Automotive Courses in Australia > Our Automotive Trade Courses in Australia > AUR50216 – Diploma of Automotive Technology

blocks.text: The Diploma of Automotive Technology is designed for students working toward senior technical and supervisory roles in the automotive industry. The course covers advanced vehicle systems, workshop management, and technical leadership across mechanical, electrical, and diagnostic disciplines.
Learn more about AUR50216 – Diploma of Automotive Technology →

sections.heading: Automotive Courses in Australia > Career Outcomes After Automotive Courses in Australia

blocks.text: Automotive qualifications open pathways into a wide range of roles, though the exact position you’re ready for depends on the level completed, your practical experience, and the type of workshop or business.

A qualification builds the practical and theoretical foundation employers look for, but most diagnostic and supervisory roles are built through a combination of study and real workshop experience over time.

School leavers wanting to start a hands-on trade career
International students seeking a practical, Automotive Course in Australia
Technicians wanting to formalise or upgrade their skills
Career changers moving into the automotive industry
Anyone wanting to progress into a diagnostic or workshop supervisory role

sections.heading: Automotive Courses in Australia > Frequently Asked Questions

blocks.text: 1. What is the difference between Certificate III and Certificate IV in automotive courses?

Certificate III in Light Vehicle Mechanical Technology focuses on foundational mechanical and servicing skills. Certificate IV in Automotive Mechanical Diagnosis builds on these with a focus on advanced fault-finding and diagnostic work.
2. Which automotive course should I start with?

If you’re new to the industry, start with the Certificate III in Light Vehicle Mechanical Technology to build trade skills. If you already have mechanical experience, the Certificate IV in Automotive Mechanical Diagnosis or Diploma of Automotive Technology may be a better entry point.
3. Do I need mechanical experience to study these automotive courses?

Entry requirements vary by qualification level. Some students enter higher-level courses after completing a lower certificate, while others may enter based on relevant experience. Contact our admissions team to discuss the best entry point for your background.
4. Can international students study automotive courses in Australia at Austra College?

Yes. Austra College is CRICOS-registered (RTO Code: 40336 | CRICOS Code: 03187D) and approved to deliver nationally recognised Automotive Course in Australia training to international students, with campuses in Adelaide, Melbourne, Sydney, and Perth.
5. Are automotive courses only about engine repair?

No. While engine and mechanical systems are core to these courses, students also learn about electrical systems, diagnostics, workshop safety, and — at Diploma level — workshop supervision and technical leadership.
6. What can I do after completing the Diploma of Automotive Technology?
Graduates may pursue senior technician or workshop supervisory roles, or continue into further study or specialist manufacturer training, depending on the pathway available.
7. Does completing an automotive course guarantee a job?
No. A qualification builds the skills and knowledge employers look for, but career outcomes depend on individual experience, the job market, and employer requirements at the time.

sections.heading: Course Overview: Certificate III in Joinery

blocks.text: The CPC31920 Certificate III in Joinery develops practical joinery skills for residential and commercial applications. This qualification covers manufacturing and assembling joinery components, processing materials with static and computer-controlled machinery, and producing stair components. Training includes using carpentry tools, handling materials, reading plans and specifications, carrying out measurements and calculations, manufacturing components for doors and windows, and assembling and installing stairs. Licensing, legislative, regulatory or certification requirements may differ between states and territories. Consult the relevant state or territory regulatory authority to confirm the requirements that apply.

blocks.text: The CPC31920 Certificate III in Joinery is suitable for students seeking to develop joinery skills through classroom and practical training. The course combines workplace safety, communication, measurements and plan reading with manufacturing, assembly and installation activities. Students learn to manufacture joinery components, use computer-controlled and static machinery, produce components for doors and windows, manufacture stair components and package manufactured products for transport. blocks.text: Demonstration of Competence through Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL)
Learners can demonstrate competency through formal, non-formal and informal learning:

Formal learning refers to learning that takes place through a structured program of instruction and is linked to the attainment of an AQF qualification or statement of attainment (for example, a certificate, diploma or university degree);

Non-formal learning refers to learning that takes place through a structured program of instruction, but does not lead to the attainment of an AQF qualification or statement of attainment (for example, in-house professional development programs conducted by a business); and

Informal learning refers to learning that results through the experience of work-related, social, family, hobby or leisure activities (for example the acquisition of interpersonal skills developed through several years as a sales representative).

Learners are encouraged to apply for RPL before or immediately after formal enrolment but before the facilitated delivery of units to ensure that they do not miss any class/workshop opportunities offered should they be unsuccessful in the RPL process.

sections.heading: Leadership and Management Courses in Australia > Frequently Asked Questions

blocks.text: 1. Do I need to already be in a management role to study these courses?

Not necessarily. The Certificate IV in Leadership and Management is designed for people stepping into their first supervisory role, so you don’t need to already be a manager to enrol — some workplace exposure to leading others is helpful, though.
2. Is a leadership and management course the same as an MBA or business degree?

No. These are vocational qualifications focused on practical, on-the-job leadership and management skills, whereas an MBA or business degree is a higher education qualification with a broader academic and theoretical focus.
3. Can I study while working full-time?
Study arrangements vary by intake and course structure. Speak with our admissions team about current timetable options if you need to balance study around work.
4. What's the difference between the Diploma and the Graduate Diploma?

The Diploma of Leadership and Management focuses on department or team-level management skills, while the Graduate Diploma of Management (Learning) is a more senior qualification focused on organisational learning, development, and strategic leadership.
5. Will this course help me move into a different industry?
Leadership and management skills are transferable across industries, so many students use these qualifications to move from a technical or operational role into a management career in a new sector.
6. Can international students study business courses in Australia at Austra College?

Yes. Austra College is CRICOS-registered (RTO Code: 40336 | CRICOS Code: 03187D) and approved to deliver nationally recognised training to international students, with campuses in Adelaide, Melbourne, Sydney, and Perth.
7. Does finishing a management course guarantee a promotion?
No. A qualification builds the leadership skills and knowledge employers value, but promotions and career outcomes depend on individual performance, workplace opportunity, and employer decisions.

blocks.text: Demonstration of Competence through Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL)
Learners can demonstrate competency through formal, non-formal and informal learning:

Formal learning refers to learning that takes place through a structured program of instruction and is linked to the attainment of an AQF qualification or statement of attainment (for example, a certificate, diploma or university degree);

Non-formal learning refers to learning that takes place through a structured program of instruction, but does not lead to the attainment of an AQF qualification or statement of attainment (for example, in-house professional development programs conducted by a business); and

Informal learning refers to learning that results through the experience of work-related, social, family, hobby or leisure activities (for example the acquisition of interpersonal skills developed through several years as a sales representative).

Learners are encouraged to apply for RPL prior to or immediately after formal enrolment but prior to the facilitated delivery of units to ensure that they do not miss any learning opportunities offered should they be unsuccessful in the RPL process.

sections.heading: Course Overview : Certificate III in Stonemasonry

blocks.text: The CPC32320 Certificate III in Stonemasonry helps you develop practical stonemasonry skills with a focus on heritage, conservation and restoration. This qualification covers working with sandstone, limestone, marble and other stone products to create, finish and restore stonework. Training includes using stonemasonry tools and equipment, reading plans, shaping and laying stone, constructing stone arches and stairs, and applying conservation principles to heritage stonework.

cyber security: protecting sensitive data and information through security architecture, and developing disaster recovery and contingency plans

sections.heading: SIT50422 Diploma of Hospitality Management > Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) and Credit Transfers (CT)

blocks.text: Demonstration of Competence through Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL)
Learners can demonstrate competency through formal, non-formal and informal learning:

Formal learning refers to learning that takes place through a structured program of instruction and is linked to the attainment of an AQF qualification or statement of attainment (for example, a certificate, diploma or university degree);

Non-formal learning refers to learning that takes place through a structured program of instruction, but does not lead to the attainment of an AQF qualification or statement of attainment (for example, in-house professional development programs conducted by a business); and

Informal learning refers to learning that results through the experience of work-related, social, family, hobby or leisure activities (for example, the acquisition of interpersonal skills developed through several years as a sales representative).

Learners are encouraged to apply for RPL before or immediately after formal enrolment but before the facilitated delivery of units to ensure that they do not miss any class/workshop opportunities offered should they be unsuccessful in the RPL process.
To learn more about how RPL is conducted, please refer to the following documents:

blocks.text: Demonstration of Competence through Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL)
Learners can demonstrate competency through formal, non-formal and informal learning:

Formal learning refers to learning that takes place through a structured program of instruction and is linked to the attainment of an AQF qualification or statement of attainment (for example, a certificate, diploma or university degree);

Non-formal learning refers to learning that takes place through a structured program of instruction, but does not lead to the attainment of an AQF qualification or statement of attainment (for example, in-house professional development programs conducted by a business); and

Informal learning refers to learning that results from the experience of work-related, social, family, hobby or leisure activities (for example, the acquisition of interpersonal skills developed through several years as a sales representative).

Learners are encouraged to apply for RPL before or immediately after formal enrolment but before the facilitated delivery of units to ensure that they do not miss any class/workshop opportunities offered should they be unsuccessful in the RPL process.

sections.heading: Course Overview - Certificate III in Commercial Cookery

blocks.text: The Certificate III in Commercial Cookery reflects the role of cooks who use a wide range of well-developed cookery skills and sound knowledge of kitchen operations to prepare food and menu items. Using discretion and judgement, they work with some independence and under limited supervision using plans, policies and procedures to guide work activities.
Completion of this qualification contributes to recognition as a trade cook.
This qualification provides a pathway to work as a cook in organisations such as restaurants, hotels, clubs, pubs, cafes, and coffee shops.
The skills in this qualification must be applied in accordance with Commonwealth and State or Territory legislation, Australian standards and industry codes of practice.

sections.heading: Course Overview - Certificate III in Commercial Cookery > Entry Requirements > Other Conditions :

blocks.text: Students are required to invest, on average, 4-5 hours a week of guided learning during the training weeks, and this does not include the term breaks.
All students are required to purchase their own chef uniform, knife set, safety boots and associated cooking equipment before participating in any kitchen or practical training sessions.
Entry into the commercial kitchen without the full chef uniform and required tools will not be permitted under any circumstances.
This is a mandatory requirement to ensure compliance with workplace health and safety regulations and to maintain professional industry standards.
Students enrolling in Certificate III in Commercial Cookery must possess a reasonable level of physical fitness.
The course involves working in a fast-paced commercial kitchen environment, requiring stamina, coordination, and attention to detail.

Tasks may include standing for extended periods, lifting and carrying bulk ingredients, working in hot environments, repetitive food preparation activities, and the safe handling of knives and kitchen equipment.

blocks.text: This policy outlines the systematic and compliant enrolment process at Austra College. It ensures that all
prospective students are enrolled only after completing the required pre-enrolment procedures and that all
relevant data is collected, verified, and stored in alignment with Outcome Standards 2.1 and 2.2. The process
supports fair, transparent, and well-informed student admission decisions. It also aligns with the requirements
of Standard 3 of the National Code 2018.

offered by Austra College. It also applies to staff involved in student enrolment, administration, support, and
delivery training.

blocks.text: Demonstration of Competence through Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL)
Learners can demonstrate competency through formal, non-formal and informal learning:

Formal learning refers to learning that takes place through a structured program of instruction and is linked to the attainment of an AQF qualification or statement of attainment (for example, a certificate, diploma or university degree);

Non-formal learning refers to learning that takes place through a structured program of instruction, but does not lead to the attainment of an AQF qualification or statement of attainment (for example, in-house professional development programs conducted by a business); and

Informal learning refers to learning that results through the experience of work-related, social, family, hobby or leisure activities (for example the acquisition of interpersonal skills developed through several years as a sales representative).

Learners are encouraged to apply for RPL before or immediately after formal enrolment but before the facilitated delivery of units to ensure that they do not miss any class/workshop opportunities offered should they be unsuccessful in the RPL process.

sections.heading: Document text

blocks.text: Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) Application
Form
Purpose
The purpose of this document is to provide you with the instructions to complete your application for RPL.
Your assessor will explain the requirements to ensure that you fully understand the criteria that will be used to
determine whether your application for RPL is granted.
Tips and Hints to Help You Prepare for RPL
To have skills formally recognised in the national system, assessors must make sure you have the skills and
knowledge to meet the industry standard. This means you must be involved in a careful and comprehensive process
that covers the content of all unit/s or qualification/s you can be recognised for.
Assessment happens in a variety of ways. Being prepared can save you valuable time and hassle and make the RPL
process stress-free for you.
Here are some tips and hints for you:
1. Be prepared to talk about your job roles and your work history. Bring a resume or jot down a few points about
where you have worked, either paid or unpaid, and what you did there.
2. Bring your position description and any performance appraisals you may have had in the past.
3. Consider the possibilities for workplace cont act. Are you in a workplace that is supporting your goals to get
qualified? Would you feel comfortable to have the assessor contact your workplace or previous workplaces so
your skills can be validated?
4. Think about who can confirm your skill level. Think about current or recent supervisors who have seen you
work in the past 18 months and will be able to confirm your skills. The assessor will need to contact them. You
may also have community contacts or even clients themselves who can vouch for your skills level.
5. Collect any certificates from in-house training or formal training you have done in the past.
6. You can speak with our assessors about other ways you can show your skills. These could be letters from
employers, records of your professional developme nt sessions, employers or clients in related industries or
government agencies, acknowledgements, workplace forms (as long as they don’t show client details) or
other relevant documents.
What is evidence?
Evidence is information that we collect that provides proof of your competency. The term ‘evidence’ applies to
anything you produce to verify your skills, knowledge and experience. The evidence will be matched to the training
package requirements of the unit/s.
The purpose of evidence is to show your RPL assessor that you have the skills and knowledge to meet the
competency requirements and industry standards.

sections.heading: Course Overview: Certificate III in Wall and Ceiling Lining

blocks.text: The CPC31220 Certificate III in Wall and Ceiling Lining develops skills for applying and fixing linings to non-structural walls and ceilings in residential and commercial construction . The course combines common construction skills with specialist wall and ceiling lining training. Students learn to fix plasterboard wall and ceiling sheets, install battens and wet area sheets, finish plasterboard joints, cut and fix cornices, assemble partitions, construct bulkheads, and install suspended ceilings and dry wall passive fire-rated systems. Occupational titles may include wall and ceiling liner, drywaller and plasterer. Completion of this qualification does not guarantee employment. Licensing, legislative, regulatory and certification requirements may vary between states and territories. Contact the relevant regulatory authority to confirm the requirements that apply.

blocks.text: Demonstration of Competence through Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL)
Learners can demonstrate competency through formal, non-formal and informal learning:

Formal learning refers to learning that takes place through a structured program of instruction and is linked to the attainment of an AQF qualification or statement of attainment (for example, a certificate, diploma or university degree);

Non-formal learning refers to learning that takes place through a structured program of instruction, but does not lead to the attainment of an AQF qualification or statement of attainment (for example, in-house professional development programs conducted by a business); and

Informal learning refers to learning that results through the experience of work-related, social, family, hobby or leisure activities (for example the acquisition of interpersonal skills developed through several years as a sales representative).

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions

blocks.text: 1. What is SIT60322 – Advanced Diploma of Hospitality Management?

SIT60322 – Advanced Diploma of Hospitality Management is a nationally recognised qualification designed to develop advanced hospitality operations, leadership and strategic business management skills.
2. What skills will I develop during this course?
Students develop skills in business planning, financial management, budgeting, marketing, recruitment, staff performance, workplace safety, customer service and hospitality operations.
3. How long does the Advanced Diploma of Hospitality Management take?
The course is delivered full-time over 104 weeks, including 80 weeks of training and 24 weeks of scheduled holiday breaks.
4. How many units are included in SIT60322?
Students must successfully complete 33 units of competency, consisting of 14 core units and 19 elective units.
5. Does the course include practical training?
Yes. The course combines classroom sessions, self-directed study, theory assessments and practical assessments conducted in a simulated workplace environment.
6. Is work placement included in the course?
Yes. Students are required to complete 192 hours of work placement at a site allocated by Austra College. This enables students to apply their skills within an operational hospitality environment.
7. What career pathways may be available after completing SIT60322?

Graduates may pursue roles such as operations manager, area manager, food and beverage manager, café manager, club manager, executive housekeeper, motel manager or rooms division manager. Completion of the qualification does not guarantee employment.
8. Where is the course delivered?
Austra College lists delivery locations in Adelaide, Melbourne, Sydney and Perth. Available training facilities and delivery arrangements may vary between locations.
9. Can I continue studying after completing this qualification?
Yes. Graduates may consider progressing to a Bachelor of Hospitality Management or another relevant higher education qualification offered by an eligible education provider.
10. Can I apply for Recognition of Prior Learning or credit transfer?

Yes. Students with relevant previous qualifications, training or hospitality experience may apply for Recognition of Prior Learning or credit transfer. Supporting evidence must be provided and assessed according to Austra College’s policies.

sections.heading: Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) and Credit Transfers (CT)

blocks.text: Demonstration of Competence through Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL)
Learners can demonstrate competency through formal, non-formal and informal learning:

Formal learning refers to learning that takes place through a structured program of instruction and is linked to the attainment of an AQF qualification or statement of attainment (for example, a certificate, diploma or university degree);

Non-formal learning refers to learning that takes place through a structured program of instruction, but does not lead to the attainment of an AQF qualification or statement of attainment (for example, in-house professional development programs conducted by a business); and

Informal learning refers to learning that results through the experience of work-related, social, family, hobby or leisure activities (for example the acquisition of interpersonal skills developed through several years as a sales representative).

Learners are encouraged to apply for RPL before or immediately after formal enrolment but before the facilitated delivery of units to ensure that they do not miss any class/workshop opportunities offered should they be unsuccessful in the RPL process.

sections.heading: 1. Purpose

blocks.text: To ensure Austra College systematically monitors the academic progress of all international students against
the training timetable and assessment schedule provided at course commencement and proactively
intervenes to support those at risk of not completing their course within the duration recorded on their
Confirmation of Enrolment (coe).
This policy ensures compliance with Standard 8 of the National Code of Practice for Providers of Education
and Training to Overseas Students 2018 (National Code 2018).

sections.heading: 2. Scope

sections.heading: 5. Policy Statement

blocks.text: Austra College is committed to ensuring that all international students have the opportunity and support to
complete their qualification within the expected duration recorded on their Confirmation of Enrolment
(coe).
This policy establishes a structured approach to monitoring course progress, identifying students at risk,
implementing intervention strategies, and reporting unsatisfactory progress where required.
Pre-Commencement Information
Before course commencement, Austra College will inform students of:
Course progress monitoring requirements
Study period expectations
Intervention strategies
Reporting obligations.
This information will be provided through:
The Written Agreement / Letter of Offer

sections.heading: 5. Policy Statement

blocks.text: Student orientation
The Student Handbook.
Monitoring Academic Progress
Student course progress is monitored through:
Monthly progress checks conducted by trainers and student support staff
Formal quarterly course progress reviews.
Monitoring includes review of:
Assessment submissions
Unit completion outcomes
Student engagement
Placement progress where applicable.
All outcomes are recorded in the Student Management System (SMS).
The training timetable aligns with the Training and Assessment Strategy (TAS) to ensure that students
remain on track to complete the course within their coe duration.
Monitoring Standard Units
For units that do not require work placement: A student is considered to be making satisfactory progress
when the unit is marked Competent (C) by the end of the study period scheduled on the training timetable.
A student may be identified as At Risk where:
The unit is not completed within the scheduled study period
The student receives a Not Yet Competent (NYC) outcome
Required assessments are not submitted.
Monitoring Placement Units
Placement Units consist of two components.
Stage 1 — Theory Assessment: The theory assessment must be completed before the student commences
work placement.
Stage 2 — Workplace Practical Assessment: The practical component is assessed during or after the work
placement period.
Course progress monitoring for Placement Units includes:
Completion of theory assessments prior to placement
Confirmation that work placement has commenced
Completion of workplace practical assessments following placement.
A student may be identified as At Risk where:
Theory assessments remain incomplete before placement
The student is not placement-ready

sections.heading: 5. Policy Statement

blocks.text: Work placement does not commence as scheduled
Workplace practical assessments remain incomplete following placement.
A Placement Unit is considered fully complete only when both theory and workplace practical assessments
are marked Competent.
Intervention Strategies
Austra College will proactively identify and support students who are At Risk.
Intervention strategies may include:
Additional academic support
LLND support
Tutoring or mentoring
Revised assessment schedules
Counselling referral.
Each intervention will be documented through an Individual Intervention Plan (IIP).
Reporting Unsatisfactory Course Progress
A student may be considered to have unsatisfactory course progress where they fail to achieve satisfactory
course progress across two consecutive study periods while an intervention plan has been implemented.
Where this occurs the College will:
Issue a Notice of Intention to Report (NOIR)
Provide the student with 20 working days to access the Complaints and Appeals process.
The student will only be reported through PRISMS where:
The student does not access the appeals process within the required timeframe; or
The appeals process confirms the College decision; or
The student withdraws from the appeals process.
Course Duration Extensions
Austra College may extend a student's course duration only where:
Compassionate or compelling circumstances exist
An intervention strategy has been implemented
An approved deferment or suspension has occurred.
Any variation to course duration will be reported through PRISMS, and the student will be advised to contact
the Department of Home Affairs regarding potential visa implications.
Compliance and Student Advice
Where a student's enrolment duration changes, Austra College will advise the student in writing to contact
the Department of Home Affairs to determine whether a new student visa is required.
All advice regarding visa implications and reporting obligations will be documented.

sections.heading: Overview

blocks.text: CRICOS Course Code: 120631D
The CPC31420 Certificate III in Construction Waterproofing is designed for students who want to develop skills used in waterproofing for residential and commercial construction work.

Students learn how to prepare surfaces, handle waterproofing materials, use waterproofing tools and equipment, apply waterproofing systems to internal and external wet areas, carry out remedial waterproofing processes, and assess waterproofing work.
Occupational titles may include:
Waterproofer
Construction Waterproofing Technician
Specialist Waterproofing Contractor
Construction Trades Assistant
It is not intended to indicate that an individual will gain immediate employment on completion of this qualification.

sections.heading: Admission Requirements

blocks.text: There are no mandatory training package entry requirements for this qualification at the time of publication on training.gov.au. However, Austra College requires applicants to meet the following admission requirements before enrolment:
Minimum age of 18 years.
Satisfactory completion of Year 10 or higher from the applicant’s home country.
English language evidence for international students may include one of the following Austra College accepted options:

Note: Results older than two years are not acceptable (for offshore applicants).
OR
Evidence that the applicant has studied in English for at least five years in Australia, Canada, New Zealand, Republic of Ireland, South Africa, United Kingdom, or the United States.
OR

Evidence that, within two years of their application date, they have successfully completed in Australia a foundation course or a senior secondary certificate of education or successfully completed substantial components (50% or more units according to the training package) IV qualification or higher level qualification, from the Australian Qualifications Framework on a student visa.
OR

Applicants originating from student visa assessment levels 1 and 2 countries without the required IELTS or equivalent score must undertake the Language, Literacy, Numeracy (LLN) and Digital (D) literacy test. For further information on student visa assessment levels visit Department of Home Affairs’ website at www.homeaffairs.gov.au
Pre-Training Review requirements:
Onshore international students must complete the Pre-Training Review, including the LLND test, to identify training needs, previous education or training, course relevance, and relevant experience.
Offshore international students must complete the Pre-Training Review, including the LLND test. This may be conducted by video call, such as Skype, or by phone.
Other conditions:
Satisfactory completion of CPCWHS1001 Prepare to work safely in the construction industry, or equivalent, is required before any construction workplace site visit.
All students must bring their PPE kits for practical classes.

Students must have a reasonable level of physical fitness, dexterity, balance, and hand-eye coordination. Practical activities may include preparing and priming surfaces, mixing and applying waterproofing materials, lifting buckets or membrane rolls, kneeling, bending, squatting, sealing joints and penetrations, working in confined or elevated areas, measuring and cutting membranes, and using hand and power tools.
Students are required to invest, on average, 4 hours per week in guided learning and summative assessments during training weeks, excluding term breaks.

sections.heading: Course Overview: Diploma of Building and Construction (Building)

blocks.text: The CPC50220 Diploma of Building and Construction (Building) qualification reflects the role of building professionals who apply knowledge of structural principles, risk and financial management, estimating, preparing and administering building and construction contracts, selecting contractors, overseeing the work and its quality and managing construction work in building projects including residential and commercial with the following limitations:
Residential construction limited to National Construction Code Class 1 and 10 buildings to a maximum of 3 storeys.
Commercial construction limited to National Construction Code Class 2 to 9 buildings, Type C and B construction.
Occupational titles may include:
Builder
General Foreperson
Building Inspector

The construction industry strongly affirms that training and assessment leading to recognition of skills must be undertaken in a real or very closely simulated workplace environment. To achieve this qualification, the candidate must have access to a live building and construction workplace to meet the requirements detailed in the Assessment Requirements of core unit CPCCBC4008 Supervise communication and administration processes for building and construction projects.

Completion of the general construction induction training program specified by the model Code of Practice for Construction Work is required for any person who is to carry out construction work. Achievement of unit CPCCWHS1001 Prepare to work safely in the construction industry meets this requirement.
Builder licensing varies across States and Territories and requirements additional to the attainment of this qualification may be required.

blocks.text: Demonstration of Competence through Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL)
Learners can demonstrate competency through formal, non-formal and informal learning:

Formal learning refers to learning that takes place through a structured program of instruction and is linked to the attainment of an AQF qualification or statement of attainment (for example, a certificate, diploma or university degree);

Non-formal learning refers to learning that takes place through a structured program of instruction, but does not lead to the attainment of an AQF qualification or statement of attainment (for example, in-house professional development programs conducted by a business); and

Informal learning refers to learning that results through the experience of work-related, social, family, hobby or leisure activities (for example, the acquisition of interpersonal skills developed through several years as a sales representative).

Learners are encouraged to apply for RPL before or immediately after formal enrolment but before the facilitated delivery of units to ensure that they do not miss any learning opportunities offered should they be unsuccessful in the RPL process.

sections.heading: Overview

blocks.text: CRICOS Course CODE: 120630E

The CPC33020 Certificate III in Bricklaying and Blocklaying reflects the trade-qualified role of bricklayers, blocklayers, and pavers working across residential, commercial, and industrial construction environments.

Students develop practical skills in bricklaying, blocklaying, paving, masonry construction, setting out, working safely, reading plans, carrying out measurements, using tools and equipment, constructing masonry walls, and applying industry-standard construction techniques.
Occupational titles may include:
Bricklayer
Blocklayer
Paver
It is not intended to indicate that an individual will gain immediate employment on completion of this qualification.

sections.heading: Admission Requirements

blocks.text: There are no mandatory training package entry requirements for this qualification. However, Austra College requires applicants to meet the following admission requirements:
Minimum age of 18 years and above.
Satisfactory completion of Year 10 or higher from the applicant’s home country.
English language evidence for international students may include one of the following Austra College accepted options:

IELTS (General or Academic) | PTE Academic | TOEFL PB | TOEFL iBT | CAE Scale | ELICOS (General English)
6.0 | 50-58 | 547-587 | 78-82 | 169-175 | n/a
5.5 | 46 | 506 | 62 | 162 | +15 weeks
5.0 | 38 | 478 | 51 | 154 | +30 weeks
Note: Results older than two years are not acceptable (for offshore applicants)
OR
Evidence that they have studied in English for at least five years in Australia, Canada, New Zealand, Republic of Ireland, South Africa, United Kingdom or United States.
OR

Evidence that, within two years of their application date, they have completed in Australia a foundation course or a senior secondary certificate of education or completed substantial components (50% or more units according to the training package) of a Certificate IV qualification or higher level qualification, from the Australian Qualifications Framework on a student visa.
OR

Applicants originating from student visa assessment levels 1 and 2 countries without the required IELTS or equivalent score must undertake the Language, Literacy, Numeracy (LLN) and Digital (D) literacy test. For further information on student visa assessment levels, visit the Department of Home Affairs’ website at www.homeaffairs.gov.au
Pre-Training Review requirements:
Onshore international students must complete the Pre-Training Review, including the LLND test, to identify training needs, previous education or training, course relevance, and relevant experience.
Offshore international students must complete the Pre-Training Review, including the LLND test. This may be conducted by video call, such as Skype, or by phone.
Other conditions:
Satisfactory completion of CPCWHS1001 Prepare to work safely in the construction industry, or equivalent, is required before any construction workplace site visit.
All students must bring their PPE kits for practical classes.

Students must have a reasonable level of physical fitness and coordination, as the course involves manual handling, lifting, bending, extended standing, working with masonry materials, and using hand and power tools. Students are required to invest, on average, 1-2 hours per week in guided learning and summative assessments during training weeks, excluding term breaks.

sections.heading: 1. Purpose

blocks.text: This policy establishes the requirements and procedures for assessing and managing student transfer requests.
It ensures Vocational RTO complies with the Education Services for Overseas Students Act 2000 and the National
Code 2018 – Standard 7, while supporting students' educational interests and welfare.

sections.heading: 2. Scope

blocks.text: This policy applies to:
All international students enrolled at Vocational RTO on a student visa, and
All staff involved in the management of student enrolments and transfers.
It specifically relates to transfers prior to the completion of six (6) months of a student’s principal course.

sections.heading: 3. Definitions

blocks.text: Term Definition
Principal Course The final course in a packaged offer.
CoE Confirmation of Enrolment issued via PRISMS.
PRISMS Provider Registration and International Student Management System.
Compassionate or
Compelling Circumstances
Circumstances beyond the student’s control that impact their ability to continue
the course.

sections.heading: 4. Legislative References

blocks.text: This policy is guided by the following:
ESOS Act 2000
National Code of Practice for Providers of Education and Training to Overseas Students 2018 – Standard
Standards for RTOs 2015
National Vocational Education and Training Regulator Act 2011

sections.heading: 5. Policy Statement

blocks.text: PP52 – Student Transfer Policy

sections.heading: 5. Policy Statement

blocks.text: RTO is committed to supporting the rights of international students to transfer between education providers in a
manner that is transparent, student-focused, and fully compliant with legislative requirements under the
Education Services for Overseas Students (ESOS) Act 2000 and the National Code of Practice for Providers of
Education and Training to Overseas Students 2018 – Standard 7.
This policy outlines the principles, conditions, and procedures under which international students
may request to transfer:
To another registered provider, either before or after completing six months of their principal course of
study
From another registered provider, subject to eligibility and documented evidence, including where a
release is granted or exemptions apply
Within the RTO, to another course or program, where the transfer is educationally justified and does not
breach student visa conditions.
In alignment with Standard 7, Vocational RTO will:
Not knowingly enrol a student from another provider who has not completed six months of their
principal course unless:
o The releasing provider or course is no longer registered
o A government sponsor supports the transfer
o A sanction affects the student’s ability to continue
o A release has been granted and recorded in PRISMS
Implement and make available a documented policy and process for assessing transfer requests prior
to the six-month restriction period, clearly outlining:
o Student responsibilities, including written requests and submission of a valid Letter of Offer
o Situations in which transfers will be approved in the student’s best interests, such as:
▪ Documented compassionate or compelling circumstances
▪ Misleading conduct by an agent or provider
▪ Failure of course delivery
▪ Poor academic progress despite intervention
▪ Mismatch between course and student expectations
▪ Favourable outcome of an appeal
o Circumstances under which a transfer may be refused, such as:
▪ Unresolved support issues
▪ Financial arrears
▪ Lack of genuine academic or personal justification

sections.heading: 5. Policy Statement

blocks.text: Ensure decisions are made within 10 working days, communicated in writing, and include reasons and
advice on accessing the RTO’s Feedback, Complaint and Appeal Policy
For students under 18, ensure a transfer is only processed when:
o Written consent is provided by a parent or legal guardian; and
o The receiving provider confirms it will assume welfare responsibilities under Standard 5;
Not charge a fee for issuing a release and advise the student to contact the Department of Home Affairs
to determine if a new visa is required
Not finalise any refusal in PRISMS until:
o The student has chosen not to appeal within 20 working days
o The appeal process is complete and the outcome supports refusal
o The student withdraws from the appeal process
Maintain complete records of all transfer requests, decisions, and supporting documentation for a
minimum of two (2) years after the student ceases to be an accepted student at the RTO.
